thread:
leah-support: FYI opened ticket for Meridian about Dedicated cluster 'meridian-eu-01' hitting TPS SLOs and getting 429s. Customer reports spike at ~12:10 UTC, sustained for ~8m, then admission control started rejecting requests.

oncall-julia: taking this. any error snippets from the customer?

leah-support: customer pasted a response: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` body: `{"error":"admission_control: rejected - burst credits exhausted"}`. They also saw 503s from our edge for a short period.

mike-sre: can you grab the admission_control rejection metric? prometheus should have `redwood_admission_control_rejections_total{cluster="meridian-eu-01"}`

leah-support: pasted a quick prometheus query result from their support dump:
```
redwood_admission_control_rejections_total{cluster="meridian-eu-01"} = 412 (12:08-12:18 UTC)
redwood_tokens_per_second{cluster="meridian-eu-01"} peak = 14800 tps
redwood_tokens_per_second_slo{cluster="meridian-eu-01"} = 10000 tps
```

ryan-runtime: 14800 vs 10k SLO — yep that's a 48% overshoot. Do we have autoscaler events in that window?

deploy-bot: recent events:
```
[12:05 UTC] autoscaler: scale_up triggered from 6 -> 8 workers
[12:07 UTC] autoscaler: scale_up throttled due to insufficient GPU headroom
[12:09 UTC] admission_control: burst_credits=0
```

mike-sre: looks like autoscaler wanted to scale but cluster-level headroom prevented it (no spare nodes). Could be noisy neighbor or placement constraint. Any infra events?

leah-support: customer said they saw a large batched job start around 12:03 from internal analytics, likely a spike of long-sequence generations. They included a repro curl: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.company/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Deployment: meridian-eu-01" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-medium-13b","prompt":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":1024}'
```

oncall-julia: thanks. next steps: (1) confirm whether burst credits were exhausted in config and why they didn't refill, (2) check min_replicas/target_utilization, (3) decide temporary mitigation for the customer. I'll ask runtime for quick config dump.

ryan-runtime: pulling config now. cluster config:
```
cluster: meridian-eu-01
min_replicas: 6
max_replicas: 12
target_utilization: 0.65
burst_credit_capacity: 300_000 tokens
current_burst_credits: 0
admission_headroom_percent: 10
```

mike-sre: admission_headroom 10% means autoscaler needs 10% spare capacity to place new allocations. If cluster is tightly packed and no spare GPUs, scale will fail. Also burst_credit_capacity 300k could be depleted quickly at 14.8k tps (300k/14.8k ≈ 20s). The customer's spike lasted minutes, so expected depletion.

leah-support: customer asked why we allowed them to hit SLO without proactive warning. They want an ETA on a fix and whether we can permit a short temporary bump.

oncall-julia: propose immediate mitigations:
- lift admission_headroom to 0% temporarily to allow placement (risk: possible inter-node contention)
- bump current_burst_credits by +500k for meridian-eu-01
- set an automated alert when tokens_per_second > 11k for more than 30s

ryan-runtime: I can patch cluster settings now. Before changing headroom I want to check placement fragility: `kubectl describe nodes | grep "Allocatable"` — if nodes are at 96% GPU memory, dropping headroom may cause OOMs.

mike-sre: also recommend enabling model-variant fallback for heavy requests: route to `rw-medium-8b-quant` when queue wait > 250ms. That will keep throughput while reducing per-token cost.

leah-support: customer is ok with temporary bump and fallback. They also want postmortem and guidance on headroom + workload planning.

oncall-julia: action list:
1) ryan-runtime to increase burst credits by 500k and lower admission_headroom to 0% for 10m. (execute now)
2) mike-sre to create temporary routing rule for model-variant fallback for requests with queue_wait > 250ms.
3) leah-support to notify customer and ask for exact time windows + any correlated internal jobs.
4) ops follow-up: schedule postmortem, review autoscaler thresholds and min_replicas.

ryan-runtime: applying changes now. patch command:
```
redwoodctl clusters patch meridian-eu-01 --set burst_credit_capacity=800000 --set current_burst_credits=500000 --set admission_headroom_percent=0
```

deploy-bot: change accepted, rolling update triggered.

mike-sre: creating routing rule now. will route long-waits to rw-medium-8b-quant for 30m window.

leah-support: notified customer and escalated to account exec. customer confirmed reduced errors within 90s of change and average TPS dropped to ~9.2k after fallback.

oncall-julia: good. we'll keep admission_headroom at 0% for 10m then revert to 10% unless we see stability issues. schedule postmortem for tomorrow 10:00 UTC with runtime + SRE + support.

leah-support: noted. will include suggested long-term fixes in the postmortem: increase baseline burst_credit_capacity for meridian, consider higher min_replicas or reserved capacity for analytics windows, and improve early alerting on sustained >11k tps.

ryan-runtime: one follow-up item: we should add a wrinkle to autoscaler so it can request temporary burst credits refill from billing for committed customers (or auto-burst with grace tokens) — filing an RFC.

mike-sre: thumbs for RFC :thumbsup:

leah-support: closing loop for now. re-open if errors reappear.

oncall-julia: thanks team. tagging for postmortem: @ryan-runtime @mike-sre @leah-support.
